subjects.title: Macroscopic Anatomy & Embryology
subjects.description: Study the organisation of the human body and connect anatomical relationships with development.

subjects.title: Microscopic Anatomy, Histology & Embryology
subjects.description: Recognise cells, tissues, and organs, and connect microscopic structure with function and development.

subjects.title: Microscopic Anatomy & Embryology I
subjects.description: Build a foundation in microscopy and the four basic tissues, then explore blood, vessels, lymphoid organs, digestive, respiratory, urinary and reproductive histology, implantation and placental development.

subjects.title: Microscopic Anatomy & Embryology II
subjects.description: Connect nervous-tissue structure with neurulation, brain and spinal-cord organization, sensory and motor pathways, autonomic reflexes, endocrine organs, special senses and their developmental origins.

subjects.title: Molecular & Cell Biology
subjects.description: Explore how cells organise, communicate, divide, and maintain their genetic information.

subjects.title: Biochemistry
subjects.description: Connect molecular structure, enzyme activity, and metabolic pathways to the workings of the body.

subjects.title: Medical Physiology
subjects.description: Understand how body systems function, interact, and maintain a stable internal environment.

subjects.title: Medical Genetics
subjects.description: Study inheritance and genetic variation through connected explanations and practice.

subjects.title: Immunology
subjects.description: Explore immune recognition, responses, and memory through connected explanations and practice.

subjects.title: Microbiology & Antimicrobials
subjects.description: The existing sterilisation, disinfection and antibiotic source collection.
